source.title: Numerical Recipes in Pascal: The Art of Scientific Computing
source.year_printing: 1989 (main text, 1st Pascal ed, ISBN 9780521375160); 1990 (companion Numerical Recipes Example Book (Pascal))
pages: main text 17.5 (Relaxation Methods for Boundary Value Problems), pp.710-717
Example Book (Pascal) driver d17r1 + printed SOR solution grid, pp.217-219
source.example_name: d17r1 (driver for routine SOR) -- printed 'SOR solution grid'

problem.domain: square lattice, jmax=11 incl. boundary (interior 9x9); unit lattice spacing h=1 in the driver's dimensionless difference equation
problem.rhs_or_ic_formula: discrete 5-point Poisson: u[i+1,j]+u[i-1,j]+u[i,j+1]+u[i,j-1]-4*u[i,j] = f[i,j]; coefficients A=B=C=D=1.0, E=-4.0; source f=0 everywhere except f[6,6]=2.0 (1-based centerpoint, midl=(11 div 2)+1=6); u=0 on all boundary nodes

params._note: Driver d17r1 uses SOR with Chebyshev acceleration; the printed grid is the converged solution and equals the exact discrete-Poisson solution to the book's 2-decimal print (cross-checked to machine precision in Python, 2026-06-17).

expected.printed_precision_sig_figs: 2 decimal places (Pascal :7:2 format); ~3 sig figs at the centerpoint, ~2 sig figs on the inner rings
expected._gate_note: Printed-precision-limited gate (OQ-7F-PAS-01 documented exception). The book prints 2 decimals, so backend-vs-book relative error is bounded by 0.005/|value|: <=1.25% on the selected |value|>=0.40 points, <=1.8% on the -0.28 points. 2.0e-2 leaves headroom. The underlying exact discrete solution agrees to machine precision (Python cross-check), so a tight-gate variant is available if the test asserts against the exact discrete solve rather than the printed values.
